headline: Google's open-source Docsy documentation project is moving to the Linux Foundation, with new features aimed at AI agents.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an open-source governance move; the AI features are opt-in and experimental.
importance_line: Open-source projects that publish technical documentation could get pages that AI tools read more easily, but the AI features are optional and still experimental.
summary: The New Stack reports that Docsy, a documentation theme for the Hugo website tool that Google created in 2019 and that about 2,200 projects used by the end of 2024, is moving to the Linux Foundation, which hosts open-source projects. Erin McKean, senior developer relations engineer at Google and a member of the Docsy steering committee, announced the move in a keynote at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague, and the features that let AI tools read Docsy sites are opt-in and experimental.
notes: Read in full. The 2,200-project figure is the article's count for the end of 2024.
